tools.name: explore_opportunity
tools.title: Explore Opportunity
tools.description: Analyze a job posting against your Career KB and your stated preferences — salary band, remote/relocation, notice period. Returns an honest fit verdict (checked against the job board's own label, if you supply it), matched strengths, gaps, talking points, and a 'day in the life' brief.

posting.description: Full job posting text, or paste the raw text from a job board

notes.description: Any additional context about this opportunity

sourceFitLabel.description: The fit label the job board showed, e.g. 'LinkedIn: strong match' or 'Indeed: 62% match' — the analysis will explicitly agree or disagree with it

tools.name: research_company
tools.title: Research Company
tools.description: Set up a research brief on a company the user is applying to or interviewing with: what it does, stage, culture, interview process, and how it fits the user's target roles. The server does not browse; it returns the brief's outline plus the user's targets, and you fill it from web search when you have it, citing sources. Without web search, the brief becomes a checklist of what to look up and where. Use explore_opportunity instead to judge fit for a specific posting.

applicationId.description: Pipeline application ID for additional context

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.title: Tailor Resume
tools.description: Generate a tailored, ATS-optimized resume matched to a specific job posting using your Career KB.

focusAreas.description: Specific areas to emphasize, e.g. 'leadership, data analysis'

tools.name: generate_cover_letter
tools.title: Generate Cover Letter
tools.description: Write a compelling, personalized cover letter using your Career KB. Works from a pasted posting, from an application already in the pipeline (its cached posting, role, and notes), or from just a company and role.

posting.description: Full job posting text. Optional: without it, the cached posting from the pipeline is used, or the letter is written from the role and your history

role.description: Role title, used to find the application in the pipeline and when there is no posting

applicationId.description: Pipeline application ID, to use its cached posting and notes

tone.description: Voice of the letter. Match it to the company: professional for traditional or regulated employers, conversational for startups, enthusiastic when you genuinely want this one, concise when the posting asks for brevity.

angle.description: The key story or angle to lead with

tools.name: format_for_ats
tools.title: Format for ATS
tools.description: Format resume and application content for specific ATS systems: Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, LinkedIn, and others.

tools.name: pipeline_view
tools.title: View Application Pipeline
tools.description: Read the job application pipeline: list applications, summarize stats, surface what needs attention, or fetch one application by id. Read-only — never modifies anything.

action.description: list = all applications (filterable); stats = funnel and response-rate summary; next_actions = today's ranked digest: one start-here move, the rest of what is due, and what is coming up; get = one application by id

filterStatus.description: action=list only: show only applications in this status

filterPriority.description: action=list only: show only applications at this priority

sortBy.description: action=list only: ordering. date = most recently updated first (the default); status = funnel order, discovered through ghosted, ties broken by most recent; priority = high to low; company = A-Z; excitement = highest first.

limit.description: action=list only: maximum applications to return (1-500)

tools.name: pipeline_add
tools.title: Add Application to Pipeline
tools.description: Add one job application to the pipeline. Creates a new record; never modifies an existing one. Use pipeline_update to change an application already being tracked.

status.description: Where this one already stands, if not at the start. One of: discovered, applied, screening, interviewing, offer, negotiating, accepted, rejected, withdrawn, ghosted. Defaults to applied. Use 'discovered' for a role you have found but not applied to — it is dated as discovered rather than applied, so it will not show up as awaiting a reply.

postingText.description: Full posting text to cache, so later interview prep can reference it without the link

source.description: Where you found it: LinkedIn, Referral, Company site, etc.

referral.description: Name of the person who referred you, if any

priority.description: How hard you intend to push on this one. Defaults to medium.

excitement.description: How excited you are about the role, 1-10. Used later to compare excitement against outcomes.

salaryMin.description: Bottom of the posted or expected salary range, in whole currency units

salaryMax.description: Top of the posted or expected salary range, in whole currency units

tools.name: pipeline_update
tools.title: Update Application in Pipeline
tools.description: Update one application already in the pipeline: change its status, add a note, set a follow-up date, record a contact, log an interview round and its outcome, or record an offer and its answer deadline. Overwrites the fields you supply and leaves the rest untouched.

id.description: Application id, as returned by pipeline_add or pipeline_view

status.description: New status in the funnel. One of: discovered, applied, screening, interviewing, offer, negotiating, accepted, rejected, withdrawn, ghosted. Any forward or backward move is allowed — searches really do go from applied straight to rejected, or from ghosted back to interviewing. The one exception is an application already marked accepted, which cannot return to a live stage.

notes.description: A note to append. Existing notes are kept; this is added with today's date.

followUpDue.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to be reminded to follow up

contactName.description: Name of a person met in this process, appended to the application's contacts

interviewType.description: Type of an interview round to append

interviewDate.description: ISO date of that interview round

interviewers.description: Names of the interviewers for the round being logged, or added to the latest round if no interviewType is given

roundOutcome.description: How the round went, in the user's words (e.g. 'moved to final', 'rejected after panel'). Attaches to the round logged in this call, else to the latest round

offerBaseSalary.description: Offered base salary per year, exactly as the offer states it

offerBonus.description: Offered annual target bonus, as an amount

offerEquity.description: Equity as the offer words it, e.g. '0.1% over 4 years'

offerCurrency.description: Currency of the offer amounts; defaults to USD

offerExpiresDate.description: Date the company needs an answer by, YYYY-MM-DD. Puts the offer at the top of the daily digest as it nears

offerNotes.description: Anything else the offer states (benefits, sign-on, conditions), in the offer's own terms

tools.name: classify_email
tools.title: Classify Email
tools.description: Read a job-search email the user pasted (recruiter outreach, interview invite, assessment, rejection, offer) and extract its type, company, role, contact, dates, urgency, and next action, matched against applications already in the pipeline, with a short reply draft. Writes nothing: any pipeline change it suggests goes through pipeline_update after the user agrees.

emailContent.description: Full email content — paste subject line and body

autoUpdatePipeline.description: If true, the classification includes the specific pipeline field changes it implies, so you can review them before anything is written. This tool only classifies — it never writes.

tools.name: prepare_interview
tools.title: Prepare Interview
tools.description: Prep the user for one upcoming interview: an opening pitch, STAR stories built from their real Career KB, likely questions for that round, questions to ask, and the concerns to get ahead of. Finds the application by id or company name and uses its posting, rounds, and contacts. For a later round in a process already under way, call interview_arc too so the prep doesn't repeat ground covered. Writes nothing.

interviewerInfo.description: Interviewer name, title, LinkedIn — helps personalize prep

postingText.description: Job posting text for this role

focusAreas.description: Specific topics or concerns to focus on

tools.name: interview_arc
tools.title: Project Interview Arc
tools.description: Mid-process projection: reconstructs the interview arc so far — rounds completed, what each surfaced, threads left open — then projects what the NEXT round will probe, without repeating ground already covered.

applicationId.description: Pipeline application ID — pulls the rounds, posting, and linked journal entries for this process

company.description: Company name (if no application ID, or to match journal entries)

role.description: Role title (if no application ID, or to match journal entries)

interviewSoFarNotes.description: Freeform notes on what has happened so far — questions they asked, what you answered, where the last interview stopped

nextRoundType.description: Type of the upcoming round, if you know it. Omit and the projection will infer the likely next stage.

tools.name: evaluate_offer
tools.title: Evaluate Offer
tools.description: Analyze a job offer the user has received: total compensation year one and fully vested, how it compares to their current pay, stated targets, other offers, and any market data they supply, then what to negotiate and the exact words. Benchmarks come only from data the user gives; the server never fetches salary data. Writes nothing.

company.description: Company making the offer. Used to pull the matching application for context.

offerDetails.description: Full offer: base salary, bonus, equity, benefits, start date, title

location.description: Work location (affects cost of living calc)

currentComp.description: Your current total comp for comparison

marketData.description: Salary research from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, LinkedIn, etc.

priorities.description: What matters most: cash, equity, flexibility, title, growth?

tools.name: ingest_document
tools.title: Ingest Career Document
tools.description: Paste any career document — performance review, award email, project summary, LinkedIn recommendation — and extract structured achievements for your Career KB. Extraction only: it reads what you paste and returns YAML for review. Writing that YAML to disk is a separate, explicit step with save_career_section.

associatedRole.description: Job role this document relates to

datePeriod.description: Time period this covers, e.g. '2023 Q1' or '2022-2023'

tools.name: generate_rejection_response
tools.title: Generate Rejection Response
tools.description: Draft a short reply to a rejection the user received: keep the door open, ask for feedback, or decline politely, plus an alternative and a LinkedIn note. If you pass applicationId, this also sets that application's status to `rejected` in your pipeline — it does not only write a draft. Leave applicationId out when the user only wants the words.

applicationId.description: Pipeline application ID. Supplying it fills in the company and role from the pipeline AND marks that application `rejected`. Leave it out to draft a reply and change nothing.

company.description: Company that sent the rejection. Filled in automatically when applicationId is given.

role.description: Role you were rejected for. Filled in automatically when applicationId is given.

rejectionContent.description: The rejection email or message content

responseGoal.description: What you want the reply to achieve: stay on good terms for future roles, ask why you were passed over, decline politely, or signal you would still take another opening there.

hadGoodRapport.description: Did you have positive interactions during the process?

tools.name: capture_insight
tools.title: Capture Career Insight
tools.description: Record a durable career signal to your journal — what an interview surfaced, why an offer felt right or wrong, the pattern behind a rejection, fresh proof of a skill. Append-only; over time these compound into the real shape of your career and enrich future resume, interview, and fit work.

type.description: What kind of signal this is

summary.description: One-line durable takeaway — the thing worth keeping

applicationId.description: Pipeline application ID this relates to

company.description: Company this insight relates to, if any. Lets later prompts surface it when you work on that company again.

role.description: Role this insight relates to, if any.

signals.description: Recurring strengths, gaps, or keywords to track over time

sentiment.description: Honest emotional read — 'hard' is valid and worth recording

tools.name: save_career_section
tools.title: Save Career KB Section
tools.description: Write one section of the Career KB to disk. This is how the Career KB gets populated — ingest_document and the resume tools only read and extract. Replaces the whole section, so send the complete list you want stored, not just new entries. A save that would drop stored entries or achievements is refused and names them, unless `replace` is true. The previous version is kept as a timestamped .bak next to it.

section.description: Which part of the Career KB to write. 'profile' is a single object; every other section is a list.

replace.description: Set true only when the user has confirmed that entries should be removed, or that an unreadable section file should be overwritten. Without it, a save that would drop stored entries is refused and the refusal lists them.

tools.name: harvest_evidence
tools.title: Harvest Evidence From a Project
tools.description: Read a local project's git history and report what you measurably did there — months active, files and file types touched, your share of commits, test ratio — each with the command that produced it. Use it when the user cannot remember what they shipped, is writing a résumé bullet for a project, or needs proof of a skill. It reports counts and asks the questions a commit log cannot answer; it never invents achievements and never writes to the Career KB.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory (the git repository root)

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to look back to. Defaults to two years ago.

authorEmail.description: Email to attribute commits to. Defaults to that repository's own git user.email. Pass it when you commit there under a different address, or the counts will be zero.

tools.name: check_setup
tools.title: Check Career Compass Setup
tools.description: Health-check this Career Compass install and report everything at once: whether a newer version has shipped, whether your data directory exists and is writable, which Career KB sections are filled in, whether the pipeline file parses, leftover temp files, and whether the dashboard is running. Every finding comes with the one command that fixes it. Run this first whenever something seems wrong, or right after an install or upgrade.

checkForUpdates.description: Whether to ask the public npm registry which version is current. Off by default: pass true only when the user asks about updates or versions. This is the only outbound network call Career Compass ever makes: an unauthenticated GET for the package name, sending nothing about you or your data.

dashboardPort.description: Which loopback port to check for a running dashboard. Matches `career-compass-mcp dashboard --port`; the default is 3141.
